newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban say foreign minister to visit Iran.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban say foreign minister to visit Iran.

text.p: A spokesman for Afghanistan's Taleban militia said on Friday that Iran had invited the Islamic movement's foreign minister to Tehran to try to improve strained relations, an Afghan news service reported.

The Taleban's deputy foreign minister, Mullah Abdul Jalil, told the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) that Foreign Minister Mullah Mohammad Ghous would go to Tehran and urge Iran to stop what he called its assistance to the Taleban's foes.
Jalil said no date had been set for the visit, which would be the first to Tehran by a senior Taleban leader since the Islamic militia captured Kabul on September 27.
AIP said Ghous would call on Iran to recognise the Taleban administration in Kabul in talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati and other Iranian officials.
Iran, which has often criticised the Sunni Moslem Taleban, has continued to recognise the government of ousted President Burhanuddin Rabbani, but denies helping any Afghan faction.

The Taleban are fighting forces loyal to Rabbani's military commander Ahmad Shah Masood and those of General Abdul Rashid Dostum on frontlines about 40 km (25 miles) north of Kabul and in remote northwestern provinces of Afghastan.
Attempts by the United Nations to broker a ceasefire between the warring factions have so far been unsuccessful.
